snippet.title: 'We Have To Know Why': Philanthropist Priscilla Chan’s Bold Bet On Rare Disease
snippet.description:
In just a decade, rare disease groups have gone from not understanding certain genetic mutations to bringing gene therapies into clinical trials. Priscilla Chan joins Becky Quick to discuss rare disease research, personalized medicine and how AI could help advance biomedicine and science.

Chan and her husband, Mark Zuckerberg, the founder of Meta, co-founded the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI) and Biohub, both with a core mission of curing, preventing, or managing all disease. Drawing on her background as a pediatrician, Chan explains how rare disease groups are building research programs, patient registries and clinical trials, and how this work could point to new approaches for treating diseases more broadly.

In this episode:
00:26 Introduction
03:02 Priscilla’s Road to Rare
13:07 Building the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative
20:20 Getting Back to Basics
30:30 Funding Rare Disease Pioneers

snippet.title: Holiday deals: Can you trust AI to find them?
snippet.description:

snippet.description:
President Donald Trump on Friday holds a news conference from the White House after returning from the APEC summit. 

The highlight of this week’s APEC summit in Shenzhen was a trilateral meeting Thursday between Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. The three leaders, meeting together for the first time, reaffirmed interests in reducing nuclear risks and plans to increase oil production.
